notes.title: Deep Discount Celebrating Tidal Shock's 1.0 Release
notes.notes:
In celebration of Tidal Shock's 1.0 Release out of Early Access, we're putting our whole catalog on sale!

Plus, we're releasing two new Debris + Tidal Shock bundles: 

The Dip Your Toes Bundle is a tentative sampler platter of our two underwater experiences, while the Deep Dive Bundle is perfect if you're ready to take the plunge into two wildly different games - the chilling depths of Debris and the neon chaos of Tidal Shock.

It's a deal that fans of underwater fun won't want to miss. See you in the depths! 🌊

notes.title: Debris 2.0.1 - Minor Stability Update
notes.notes:
Thanks everyone for the feedback thus far on Debris co-op. It’s been awesome to see people playing together on Twitch, so we’ll keep an eye on that. This new build addresses some networking issues we’ve seen including one where players would drop connections during level transitions.

If you’re still having issues joining a friend’s hosted game, here's something to try that solved the issue in a few cases (Windows-only for now):

Select Debris in your Steam library and right click > Properties
Go to Local Files and click Browse Local Files
Right click debris.exe and go to Compatibility
Check "Run this program as an administrator"
Click Apply
Go back to your Steam library and relaunch Debris

Important: Make sure you launch the game from Steam!

As always, keep us posted if you have any issues and thanks for playing!

notes.title: Patch notes - 1.1.1
notes.notes:
Latest update just pushed with a few small but sought-after options:

Additional options in Settings menu

Enable/disable Raw Input for mouse/controller. This will remove any smoothing/acceleration on cursor movement.
Enable/disable Motion Blur.
Enable/disable HUD Warp.

We’ve also re-introduced some special creatures, fixed a bunch of small bugs (like one where music would double up between chapters and reloads) and tweaked mouse control based on player feedback.

Still working on larger updates to come. Thanks again for the feedback and comments!

notes.title: Debris 1.1 - The Ice Update
notes.notes:
https://steamusercontent-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/857235318921103637/BB930B19496927339327881C9199446C05B3ECDA/

The Nice Update
Hey everyone! Thanks again for all the post-launch feedback and we’re very excited to announce our first update. We’ve tried to address as many things as possible, but we’re still working on a few things. Lots new features and fixes:

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30014188/1da7eecc45e16517512d7f24e07610d3b89de791.png

Brand new ice shader and smoothed ice
This is a big one. We’re finally releasing our transparency-having, refraction-doing ice shader. To see the new shader, update and make sure you’re on the Fantastic quality setting (unfortunately this is PC-only). We’ve also re-surfaced all the ice geometry in the game, getting rid of some bothersome reversed normals and other artifacts along the way. You’ll have the new geometry on any quality setting on Mac & PC.

Revised creature movement
We’ve done a complete pass on creature animations and they should be swimming smoothly and attacking accurately. We’ve also adjusted movement and attack speeds for creatures, so stay vigilant under the ice!

Balance changes
We’ve made a few tweaks to make the game more intuitive while keeping it challenging. These changes include moving around debris caches, adjusting creature damage and health, and even relighting some sequences.

…and lots more!

A bunch of performance optimizations 
Fix for a bug where your camera spins around if you have a controller plugged while using the keyboard
Updated the player’s field of view to help reduce motion sickness
Support for new resolutions including Ultra Wide (21:9)
Squid AI pathing and movement updates
Support for left-handed players (I,J,K,L,U for now)
Fix for players who could swim through debris and dead fish

Thanks everyone for your support at launch and as always let us know if you have any feedback either here or in the discussion forums! Also, we’re still hard at work on co-op and hope to have it out soon!

notes.title: Quick update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, it's been great to see people playing Debris on Twitch and YouTube. So far we've really appreciated the reception, and feedback on both sides has been great to read after such a long development. Thanks to everyone for the support so far.

Right off the bat: we miscalculated our pricing. We're a very small studio and spent a lot of time trying to find the right launch price for our first original game, but we missed the mark. 

We know a lot of people are interested in the game and want everyone to give Debris a try, so we're lowering our base price a bit to reflect that. We also want to be completely transparent because we respect our customers' time and money. 

If you have any concerns/questions at all or if you already bought the game at the old price, please send us an email at support@moonraystudios.com.

But there's more! Co-op is on it's way and we've been testing a bunch internally. We've been tweaking the thruster controls for the Squid a bit but so far so good. 😀 We'll keep you posted!

notes.title: Release date update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, quick update.

Due to unforeseen complications, we have decided to push the release of Debris. Not too long, still this year. We apologize to our fans for the inconvenience and will keep you posted here and on social media.

Thanks again to all of our beta testers so far, and stay tuned for more info!
